summary.text: 爸 means “father” or “papa.” Its usual analysis is a phonosemantic compound: 父 supplies the father meaning and 巴 is proposed as a sound component. This analysis describes the word and the components; the dossier does not date when the complete graph was formed.

formation.text: Phonosemantic: 父 contributes the meaning “father,” while 巴 is proposed to cue the sound. The sound analysis compares 巴 *praː with 爸 *praː in Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese system. Because 巴’s original referent and name are unsettled, that comparison is proposed rather than independently confirmed from the object it may once have depicted.

components.text: 父 is the semantic component, contributing the father meaning. A curated oracle-style image is a modern redraw of 父 alone; it illustrates the component, not an early form of 爸. The dossier gives a transmitted Shuowen account of 父 as a family head holding a staff, but does not establish that account as the component’s original pictorial meaning here.

巴 is proposed as the phonetic component. A curated oracle-style image is a modern redraw of 巴 alone, not an attestation of 爸. The transmitted Shuowen tradition links 巴 to a giant snake, while another proposal reads early forms as a kneeling person; neither referent is established, so the picture cannot independently confirm the sound analysis.

sound.text: In Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese system, 巴 is reconstructed as *praː and 爸 as *praːs. This is the reported sound comparison behind the proposed phonetic role; the evidence does not independently establish the original name of what 巴 may have depicted.

history.text: The consulted research reports 爸 absent from Shuowen and cites a Three Kingdoms-era Guangya entry grouping 爸 with 爹 and 㸙 under the gloss “father.” This is evidence for the word’s recorded use, not a date for a physical witness or for the formation of the graph. The selected oracle-style illustrations show 父 and 巴 separately and do not establish an earlier 爸 form or a sequence of graphic change.

A historical dictionary transmits an account in which 父 was added to a father word represented by 八八 or 巴巴. Later research instead argues that the father word is phonologically from 父. These are competing explanations; the dossier does not establish the graph’s formation sequence or a whole-graph borrowing history.

uncertainties.text: The phonosemantic analysis is source-reported, but no inspected early inscription or dated sequence of the complete graph demonstrates when 父 and 巴 were combined.

巴’s early form is disputed: the transmitted Shuowen tradition associates it with a giant snake, while a modern proposal interprets forms read as 巴 as a kneeling person. Neither account establishes the original referent or name, limiting independent confirmation of its proposed sound role in 爸.

A proposed Proto-Sino-Tibetan source for the father word and the claim that 爸 preserves an older pronunciation of 父 are not independently substantiated in the dossier. The lexical relationship is separate from the proposed 巴 phonetic component.

senses.period: Three Kingdoms era (reported dating of the Guangya record)
senses.text: The consulted study reports a Guangya record glossing 爸 as “father.” The dossier does not establish a dated physical witness for that graph.
Modern reference material gives “father, papa”; the dossier does not establish a separate historical stage for the familiar “papa” sense.

limitations.text: The attested father gloss establishes use of the word but does not date the graph’s formation. The dossier does not establish a chronological development from “father” to “papa.”

overview.text: 爸 means “father” or “papa.” 父 contributes the father meaning; 巴 is proposed as a sound cue, with its original name and referent still uncertain.

components.text: 父 contributes the father meaning. Its selected oracle-style image is a redraw of this component, not an early 爸.
巴 is proposed as the sound component, though its original referent and name remain uncertain.

relationships.text: 父 contributes the father meaning in the reported phonosemantic analysis of 爸.
巴 is proposed as the sound component; the reported comparison is 巴 *praː and 爸 *praːs in Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese system, though 巴’s original name is not established.
